evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs on pull_request only with `contents: read` and runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` in site/. All three are real scripts in site/package.json, and build includes svelte-check. The PR-title check passes the title through env, so it is not injected. There is no pull_request_target, and the only token is github.token, used in release.yml. Every action is pinned to a major tag, not a full commit SHA: actions/checkout@v7, setup-node@v7, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5, deploy-pages@v5 (step1.patch lines 54-55, 108-115, 125, 137, 161-164). pages.yml grants `pages: write` and `id-token: write` at workflow level, so the build job gets them too instead of only deploy. It also has an unguarded `workflow_dispatch` that can run from any branch, while the push trigger is `branches: [main]`. Nothing was run or published.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 316-399) covers requirements (Node 22), install (`cd site && npm ci`), develop (`npm run dev`), test, build (including the PAGES_BASE note, which matches site/vite.config.ts:11), data contribution (issue templates that exist in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE, editing JSON in data/, stating the source) and license (MIT, LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY.md exist). Every script listed (index, fieldsets, prepare-data, sample-bullets, preview) is in site/package.json, and data/bullets/README.md exists.
evidence.s1_release: There is one consistent strategy. The version lives in site/package.json `version`, and releases are tags `v<version>` (CONTRIBUTING.md Versioning, with a SemVer bump table). release.yml checks that the tag is on main and matches package.json, takes the notes from the matching CHANGELOG section and runs `gh release create`. CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and has an [Unreleased] section. Dependabot covers npm in /site and github-actions, with `build`/`ci` prefixes and scope, which fits the convention. Conventional Commits 1.0.0 is stated with its types, and all 7 commits in commits.txt follow it (e.g. `ci: deploy the site to GitHub Pages from main`, `feat(site): ...`, `fix(site): ...`). Small inconsistency: CONTRIBUTING says CI/docs-only changes need no changelog entry, but step 1 added one.
evidence.s2_requirements: Route: router.ts parses `compare/<a>/<b>` from location.hash, so a reload works, and href.compare encodes both keys. Drawing: compare.ts `outlines` uses caseOuterProfile(adaptMetallic) and one shared viewportFor in landscape, which gives one scale, one axis and head faces at the same x. It draws two `<path>`s in one `<svg role=img aria-label='Profiles of {a} and {b}'>` using record names. Shot cartridges get null and a message. Table: dimensionsOf takes numeric cartridge-part fields with no FIELD_UNITS entry; orderedFields drops `*Tol`. The caption is `Dimensions (mm|in)`, the headers are Symbol / name A / name B / Difference, the first cell uses FIELD_LABELS, and the difference is b - a. Units follow unitSystem(): metric uses formatValue, imperial uses displayNumber(...,'in'). Cartridge.svelte adds a Label `Compare with`, a NativeSelect of the other entries by name and a `Compare` button to href.compare(key, chosen). German strings were added for every key. All requirements are met.
evidence.s2_correctness: Checked against data/cartridges/rimless/308_win.json and belted/300_win_mag.json. eMin 1.4 vs 0.94 gives a difference of -0.46: displayNumber's toPrecision(12) removes float noise without rounding the published figures. beta and delta are numbers in the data but have FIELD_UNITS entries, so they are excluded as the spec requires. Imperial differences are converted from the mm difference. Each fullSectionPath starts at the profile's head-face point, and viewportFor shares zMin and rMax, so both outlines sit on the same axis with heads aligned. Edge cases: shotshell gives no drawing, a malformed % escape falls back to the list, an unknown key rejects into the `compare.error` alert, and a record too sparse to draw (adaptMetallic throws) still shows the table.
evidence.s2_fit: It reuses @lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), @lib/geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), @lib/shapes2d (adaptMetallic, caseOuterProfile), site units.ts/units.svelte.ts, the shadcn NativeSelect/Label/Button and the existing lazy-chunk routing in App.svelte. The pure logic is in site/src/lib/compare.ts next to its test, which matches repo structure. It touches few files (App, SiteNavigation, metadata, router, i18n, Cartridge). Minor style deviations: Compare.svelte uses scoped selectors where the other route files use `:global([data-ui=...])`, and the CSS added to Cartridge.svelte is packed onto one line (`display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; ...`) while the surrounding rules are multi-line.
evidence.s2_tests: compare.test.ts runs compareRows on the real 308 Win./300 Win. Mag. records (labels, e min values, exclusion of Tol, non-mm and angle fields), lengthText and differenceText in metric and imperial including float noise and zero, outlines (shared head x, shotshell gives null). router.test.ts adds round-trip and encoding tests plus seven malformed-hash cases. Everything uses the existing Vitest setup and @lib/testing/fixtures. Gaps: nothing covers the SVG accessible name, caption or headers, or the Compare-with control (the repo has no component tests). The head-face test only compares the first M coordinate.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: compareRows now takes the union of both field sets, with `a`/`b` as `number | null`. lengthText and differenceText return '' for null. Tests check that `delta L` has b=null and `R3` has a=null, and that the empty strings come out. The changelog text and the now-inaccurate `compare.none` message were updated in both languages. Rows only B publishes are appended at the end instead of in detail-page group order. Style: step 3 has no CSS change, but Compare.svelte from step 2 already sets `th, td { text-align: right }` with `thead th:first-child, tbody th { text-align: left }` inside @layer legacy. That layer outranks base (shadcn.css:1), so the number columns and their headers are right-aligned in the final code. The commit does not mention the style point.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 added a line under `## [Unreleased]` / Added, and step 3 amended it (the feature is unreleased, which fits Keep a Changelog). The version stays 0.1.0, which matches the stated strategy of bumping only in a release PR. Commits `feat(site): ...` and `fix(site): ...` follow Conventional Commits. The code type-checks by inspection (the t() vars signature, NativeSelect forwarding id to the select, fixture paths exist), so CI's npm test and npm run build should pass, though I did not run them.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 / review criterion: GitHub Actions are pinned to major version tags (e.g. actions/checkout@v7), not full commit SHAs
Step 1 / review criterion: Pages workflow grants pages:write and id-token:write at workflow level, so the build job gets them too, and its workflow_dispatch trigger is not restricted to main
strengths: The compare feature meets every step 2 requirement and reuses lib/core, lib/geom and lib/shapes2d plus the site's units and UI components, with no duplicated logic. Values, differences and the overlaid profiles are correct for the data.

Step 1 sets out one coherent release strategy: version in site/package.json, a guarded tag-triggered release that takes notes from a Keep a Changelog CHANGELOG, Dependabot with convention-matching prefixes, and a README whose commands all exist.
Steps 2 and 3 follow that strategy: Conventional Commits, changelog entries, no ad-hoc version bump. The step 3 bug fix is minimal and tested against the exact `delta L`/`R3` case from the review.
issues: No action in the workflows is pinned to a full commit SHA; all use mutable major tags (checkout@v7, setup-node@v7, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5, deploy-pages@v5).
pages.yml gives pages:write and id-token:write to the whole workflow, build job included, instead of only the deploy job, and its workflow_dispatch trigger can run from any branch.

Step 3 made no change for the alignment point. The step 2 CSS already right-aligns the number columns and headers, but the commit does not mention the style point. Rows only B publishes are appended at the end instead of in detail-page order.
review.verdict: The compare view is correct, well integrated and tested, and the step 3 bug is fixed cleanly with the release conventions followed throughout. I would merge it once the actions are pinned to commit SHAs and the Pages permissions are scoped to the deploy job.
